column1: Appendix 8. Recommended intakes of fat, carbohydrates and protein for
adults and children over 2 years1 (without alcohol and with fibre taken
into account)
Fat
• The proportion of monounsaturated fatty acids1 should be 10 to 20% (E%) of the energy intake.
• The proportion of polyunsaturated fatty acids1 should be 5 to 10 E%, of which at least  1 E% should be n-3 fatty acids.
• The proportion of essential fatty acids, i.e. linoleic acid and alpha-linolenic acid, should be at least 3 E%, of which at least 0.5 E% should be alpha-linolenic acid.
• Pregnant and lactating women should get at least 5 E% of essential fatty acids, of which  1 E% should be n-3 fatty acids. The intake of docosahexaenoic acid, DHA (22:6 n-3), should
be 200 milligrams per day. In vegans, an adequate intake of alpha-linolenic acid ensures an adequate DHA status.
• At least two thirds of the intake of total fatty acids1 should be monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids.1
• The intake of saturated fatty acids1 should be limited to less than 10 E%.
• Trans fatty acid intake should be as low as possible.
• A total fat amount of 25–40 E% is recommended.
1 Expressed in triglycerides.
Carbohydrates and dietary fiber
• Adults: The recommended dietary fiber for adults is at least 3 g/MJ, which corresponds to at least 25 g per day for women and at least 35 g per day for men with an indicative energy
intake.
• Children: The recommended dietary fiber for children over two years of age is 2 to 3 g/MJ. For school-aged children, the intake of fibre must increase to match the intake of adults by
puberty.
• The intake of free sugar2 must be less than 10 E%.
• The recommended total amount of carbohydrates is 45 to 60 E%.
